subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw core own a minimal first-party collaboration layer for learned routing, shared knowledge, memory visibility, and budget governance, or should most of this remain plugin/ClawHub work with only narrow SDK/storage/security seams tracked in core?
rationale: The requested stack crosses product direction, core/plugin boundaries, durable state, security policy, config surface, and delegation behavior, so source inspection cannot choose the intended permanent ownership model.

options.title: Keep RFC and split approved slices
options.body: Use #35203 as the canonical umbrella while maintainers carve out narrow follow-ups for capability facts, budget governance, memory visibility, and storage/security design.

options.title: Move orchestration mostly to plugins
options.body: Route blackboard/orchestrator/workflow variants to ClawHub or external plugins and track only missing SDK, storage, visibility, or tool-policy seams in core.

options.title: Close after narrower trackers
options.body: Close the broad RFC only after selecting or creating canonical smaller issues that preserve the parts maintainers still want to evaluate.

recommendation.title: Keep RFC and split approved slices
recommendation.body: Use #35203 as the canonical umbrella while maintainers carve out narrow follow-ups for capability facts, budget governance, memory visibility, and storage/security design.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal across current sessions_spawn/multi-agent history and recent product scoping comments on related multi-agent RFCs.
